candidate_relations.reason: Glioblastoma can mimic this imaging appearance but is a malignant glial tumor, not a cryptococcal granuloma.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Alternative neoplastic diagnosis for a ring-enhancing cerebral mass

candidate_relations.reason: Corpus callosum PCNSL is an imaging differential but is lymphoid malignancy rather than cryptococcoma.
CNS toxoplasmosis can produce enhancing lesions but is caused by Toxoplasma rather than Cryptococcus.
PCNSL is a differential for an enhancing callosal mass but is not cryptococcoma.
Neurocysticercosis may cause enhancing intracranial lesions but represents Taenia solium infection, not cryptococcal disease.
A butterfly glioblastoma can involve the corpus callosum but is a neoplasm rather than cryptococcoma.
Marchiafava-Bignami disease affects the corpus callosum but is a toxic-metabolic demyelinating disorder, not a cryptococcal mass.
Astrocytoma is a tumor differential for the mass but does not identify cryptococcoma.
Cerebral lymphoma can resemble the lesion radiographically but is not cryptococcoma.
The benchmark specifies cryptococcoma, whereas this candidate provides no diagnostic entity.
Glioblastoma multiforme is an imaging differential but is pathologically distinct from cryptococcoma.
Diffuse large B-cell PCNSL involving the corpus callosum is a distinct neoplasm, not a cryptococcal granulomatous lesion.

case_quality_flags: Negative CSF India ink and fungal culture do not exclude a localized cryptococcoma; definitive pathology or cryptococcal antigen results are not supplied.
